scores.why: Layered pipeline: signed task warrants with scope narrowing, OPA access rules, a signature feed with escape decoding, checksum-validated PII and secret patterns, a real Ollama judge on input and output, fails closed. Live evaluation blocked 20 of 20 attacks with 1 false block.

Clean shared core behind OpenAI and MCP adapters, one policy snapshot per request, budget reserved then settled, Prometheus metrics and a benchmark (8.7 ms p50 without the judge). Single process with SQLite; the judge adds about 4.8 s.
Working React dashboard backed by the API; hash-chained, signed audit log with export and an offline verifier; metrics endpoint. No cost-in-money view.
193 test functions over 4.2k lines, 326 passed in recorded evidence, 8 policy tests in real OPA, plus a 48-case EN/PL live evaluation reported honestly.
Drop-in OpenAI base URL plus MCP endpoint, make targets, Docker compose with Ollama and OPA. Single node, budgets count tokens not money, local feed file.

projects.built_during_event: yes: commits 3 Oct 12:30 to 4 Oct 10:29 CEST
strengths: Real end-to-end gateway with a real local LLM judge, OPA and signed audit
Hot reload of policy and feed, keeping the last valid snapshot on a bad edit
Strong, honest test and evaluation evidence with latency numbers
weaknesses: Judge latency of about 5 s per request
No money-based budgets or rate limits; single process
Signature feed is a local file; no model-file scanning
red_flags: Detector extensions on 4 Oct were not re-run live (disclosed)
README test count (494) is above the recorded evidence (326)
projects.verdict: The strongest submission: a working, tested control layer covering most of the brief, held back by judge latency and single-node scope.

scores.why: The gateway prototype has auth, a model allowlist, an in-memory token budget, checksum PII and self-testing feed rules, but the semantic layer is a keyword-weight sum and a keyword simulation; no real model judge.
Two separate prototypes with rich diagrams and a perf script, but the cache, replicas and classifier exist only in docs.
JSONL audit and a metrics script; the dashboard is a browser-only mockup not wired to the gateway.
46 pytest functions (about 76 cases) starting real processes with allowed and blocked cases; 120 extra checks test the mockup, not the product.
Good integration guidance, but in-memory budgets, plaintext keys, no MCP, and the shown demo build lives in another repository.

calibration_note: Scored on repo contents only; Clearance's out-of-repo demo might impress live, but judges cannot audit it from the submission.
